🇲🇽🐉🔥 Mexico slapped up to 50% tariffs on China. Chinese imports rose anyway.

The numbers just came in: Chinese imports climbed 5.23% to US$42.85 billion in the first four months of 2026 — even after Mexico imposed duties of 35% to 50% across 1,463 product lines from countries without a trade deal. A roughly 15% appreciation of the peso quietly swallowed the tariffs, and Banamex says that's exactly why no generalized jump in consumer prices ever showed up.

Read it as what it always was: a signal, not a wall. The tariffs told Washington — ahead of the T-MEC review — that Mexico would "police" the supposed back door, while trade with its No. 2 partner kept flowing. China stayed China. The market routed around the politics.

That's the sovereignty lesson. When the empire demands you wall off your second-largest supplier, you can write the rule and still let a strong peso protect your own consumers. Diversification isn't obedience — it's keeping the door open on your own terms.

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico backs the Panama Canal Neutrality Protocol — as Washington keeps pressuring over the canal. "We support the Neutrality Protocol of the Panama Canal." — Claudia Sheinbaum, bilateral meeting with President Mulino Meeting Panama's president at Palacio Nacional, she called to deepen ties "based on mutual respect, dialogue and cooperation" and to strengthen CELAC. The visit included talks with 23 Mexican companies.

🇲🇽✊ "The first thing we did was write women's rights into the Constitution — they weren't fully established there." "The first thing we did was take women's rights to the Constitution, where they were not fully established." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the foundation of the feminicide law The constitutional reform on women's rights is the base for the new law: unified definition, 50–70 years, imprescriptible, zero impunity.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico ranks 12th in the 2026 World Happiness Report — first in Latin America, and the most populous nation in the top 12. "People are content — though some aren't." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the World Happiness Report Gallup places Mexico 12th of all nations, 1st in Latin America, with 133M+ people — the largest population in the top tier. INEGI's life-satisfaction score rose from 8.45 (2021) to 8.62 (2025).

🔥🇲🇽 A former Pemex director — a longtime ally — was just detained on domestic violence charges. Sheinbaum didn't flinch. "Víctor's own arrest shows that regardless of friendship or position, the law has to be enforced… we will never protect anyone who breaks the law, and even less if there is violence against women." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the detention of Víctor Rodríguez Padilla No exception for closeness or rank — the same day she sent the feminicide law to Congress.

🇲🇽⚖️ Feminicide would become imprescriptible — no statute of limitations, no amnesty, no reduced sentences, ever. "This General Law guarantees that all of it can be reduced to the maximum, and that we truly have zero impunity for feminicides." — Claudia Sheinbaum, presenting the law The crime, its punishment and reparations would never expire. Prosecutors would be bound to investigate "with reinforced due diligence" under specialized gender-perspective protocols.

🇲🇽⚖️ Mexico's first woman president sends Congress a General Law on Feminicide — 50 to 70 years, uniform across all 32 states. "As the first woman President, I took on the responsibility of protecting women from violence. The worst crime of violence against women, the worst form of discrimination and indignity, is death — feminicide." — Claudia Sheinbaum, signing the initiative The bill unifies the definition of feminicide nationwide with 19 aggravating factors. Congress takes it up in September.
